title: Karin's bone-anchored, nerve-connected Mia Hand: after more than three years of daily use her phantom pain fell from 5 to 3 and her stump pain vanished (Science Robotics case report)
summary: Swedish amputee Karin uses a bone-anchored, nerve-linked Mia Hand daily; phantom pain fell 5 to 3, stump pain gone (Sci. Robotics 2023).
account: Karin, a Swedish woman born in 1973 who lost her right hand below the elbow in a farming accident, received a neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis at Sahlgrenska University Hospital: titanium implants in the radius and ulna, severed nerves transferred to muscle grafts, and implanted electrodes feeding an embedded controller and a Prensilia Mia Hand. The study ran from September 2018 to April 2021, and the EU DeTOP consortium announced the implantation on 5 February 2019. The case report, published in Science Robotics on 11 October 2023, states that her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3, stump pain vanished, quality of life rose, and that she had used the hand in daily life for more than three years and continues to.
purpose: The prosthesis was built to give reliable control, feedback and attachment after amputation, with surgical reconstruction to add myoelectric sites and treat neuropathic pain; the reported function and pain outcomes were that purpose.
system: Transradial neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis: osseointegrated titanium implants with implanted muscle and nerve electrodes, an embedded controller, and the Prensilia Mia Hand
developer: Center for Bionics and Pain Research (Chalmers University of Technology and Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Mölndal) with Integrum AB; hand by Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna and Prensilia SRL, under the EU DeTOP project
deployer: Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Sweden (surgery led by Rickard Brånemark and Paolo Sassu)
domain: Healthcare (upper-limb prosthetics and phantom limb pain)
taxonomy_note: The daily use of the nerve-linked hand for over three years is also an accessibility gain.

ratings.reason: The paper reports phantom limb pain down from 5 to 3, stump pain from 6 to 0, sleep interference gone, EQ-5D-5L up from 0.23 to 0.63 and more than three years of daily use; Karin says the research “has given me a better life” and that she needs much less medication. Life-changing for one identifiable person, from a single-patient study without a control group.

ai_role.statement: The benefit comes from the whole neuromusculoskeletal interface, not from a learned model alone. The paper reports that in daily life the hand ran on direct control, with signals from two implanted electrodes mapped to open and close and a sustained open signal switching grasps; the decoding of six movements (100 percent completion) and of five individual fingers (up to 95 percent) was demonstrated in laboratory Motion Tests. The paper never uses the words AI or machine learning. The AI framing comes from the institutions' release (Brånemark: osseointegration, reconstructive surgery, implanted electrodes “and AI”) and from CNN (“AI algorithms inside the prosthesis interpret the signal”). Keep the record only if that framing is acceptable as the AI claim.

evidence.citation: Ortiz-Catalan M., Zbinden J., Millenaar J., et al. (2023). A highly integrated bionic hand with neural control and feedback for use in daily life. Science Robotics 8(83): eadf7360. PMID 37820004. Co-authors include Integrum AB and Prensilia SRL staff; open-access manuscript at research.chalmers.se/publication/537965.

produced_by: Osseointegrated titanium implants giving skeletal attachment and a wired path from implanted electrodes to the hand
Surgical reconstruction that transfers severed nerves to free muscle grafts, adding myoelectric sites and treating neuropathic pain
A self-contained prosthesis with an embedded controller and battery that needs no external equipment, so it can be worn all day
must_hold: The fixtures must osseointegrate; here the radial fixture failed, was removed after 5 months and reimplanted with a larger diameter
Implanted electrodes must stay within working range for years; one e-abutment screw broke after 3.5 years and was replaced
Outcomes are from one patient with no control group, so the effect size is not established beyond this case

headline: Bone-anchored Mia Hand cuts Karin's phantom pain from 5 to 3
metric: her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3, stump pain vanished

comparator.against: her own phantom limb pain and stump pain before the neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis (also a conventional prosthesis for grip precision)
comparator.after: phantom pain level 3; stump pain vanished entirely
comparator.quote: Her phantom pain level dropped from a 5 to a 3, the study said, and her stump pain vanished entirely. She said she’s also been able to sleep better.

later.note: The October 2023 coverage reports more than three years of daily use up to publication; nothing dated after the paper was found.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources.

claim_basis: Five independent news reports, the makers' peer-reviewed study and two press releases from the makers are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
